 Eagles at Commanders Injury Report
 The Eagles' offense gets good news with Saquon Barkley cleared to play.
 Oct 30, 2026 at 03:51 PM PhiladelphiaEagles.com 
 Copied! 
 RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back.
 "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is.
 "I don't want to look back and be like, I could have given it a chance and I didn't. It's kind of what I live by. So, try my best to just keep recovering, being smart. I like playing football. So, if I have the opportunity to play, I try my best to play."
 The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield.
 "You prepare like you are a starter and I have always been like that. All the years I've been in the league, just prepare like you're going to start and you won't have to get ready," Mitchell said after Friday's practice.
 Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season.
 Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys.
 "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that."
 Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks.
 On the defensive side of the ball, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have been ruled out after not participating in practice all week.
 No players are listed as questionable.

 Thursday's Injury Report
 Safety Marcus Epps was added to the Eagles' injury report on Thursday with a jaw injury that required a concussion evaluation. He was officially limited in practice.
 The team was back on the field for a full practice after a Wednesday walkthrough coming off the Monday night game against Dallas.
 Six players would not have practiced on Wednesday and those same six players did not practice on Thursday: running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), wide receiver/punt returner Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle).
 With Barkley sidelined, Jaydon Blue is the only healthy running back on the active roster. The team also has Elijah Mitchell on the practice squad. Mitchell was elevated for Monday night's game.
 "I feel like I'm very comfortable in the offense," said Blue, who was active for the Carolina game but did not play. "I've been here long enough, like I said, just learning from the vets and things like that, but I'm ready. I feel like I'm going to take advantage of every opportunity I get, but man, I'm looking forward to the opportunity."
 Blue is familiar with Sunday night's opponent in the Washington Commanders. As a rookie with the Cowboys in 2025, Blue played one of his five games against Washington.
 "They're really good on defense," Blue said. "They have some great guys over there that have a really good D-line, really good front seven, very physical DBs, so I'm looking forward to it."

 Wednesday's Injury Report
 The Eagles held a walkthrough on Wednesday in their return to the practice field ahead of Sunday night's prime-time showdown with the Washington Commanders.
 With Wednesday's practice report only an estimation, the Eagles would have been without running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), wide receiver/punt returner Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle).
 Good news for the Eagles is that outside linebacker Nolan Smith would have returned to the practice field for the first time since suffering a concussion against the Carolina Panthers in Week 6. Defensive back Michael Carter would also have returned to practice in a limited capacity, as he's been sidelined for the past two games with an abdominal injury.

 Commanders Head Coach Dan Quinn told reporters that defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw will likely not be able to play Sunday night against the Eagles due to a knee injury.
 Coming off the bye week, backup quarterback Marcus Mariota (knee) is on track to return to the lineup.
 Wide receiver Terry McLaurin is on Injured Reserve with a knee injury. The Commanders signed veteran wide receiver Van Jefferson from the practice squad to take McLaurin's roster spot.
 McLaurin is one of several Commanders who have landed on Injured Reserve since the Week 1 meeting between the teams, including linebacker Leo Chenal, running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt, outside linebacker Javontae Jean-Baptiste, and wide receiver Jaylin Lane.
